title: Security Engineer
subtitle: Cybersecurity from the SOC to the cloud - with a specialisation in securing AI systems
summary: Defend systems, detect and respond to attacks, secure cloud and applications - including AI.
expert: Thinks like an attacker and builds like a defender: detects and contains real intrusions, secures cloud, identity and applications by design, red-teams AI systems, and leads a security programme that holds up to auditors and attackers alike.

benchmarks.title: Certifications
benchmarks.detail: Security+ by the end of Foundation; CySA+ or BTL1 by the end of Intermediate; a cloud security certification (AZ-500 or AWS Security Specialty) and OSCP/PNPT/eJPT by the end of Advanced.

benchmarks.title: Public challenges
benchmarks.detail: picoCTF: 60+ challenges; Cryptopals sets 1-3; PortSwigger: all Apprentice plus 50 Practitioner labs; pwn.college: two belts.

benchmarks.title: Blue team
benchmarks.detail: Splunk Boss of the SOC: a full dataset investigated with a written report; 10 CyberDefenders or LetsDefend investigations.

benchmarks.title: AI security
benchmarks.detail: PortSwigger 'Web LLM attacks' labs completed; a red-team report on a real AI application with every finding fixed.

benchmarks.title: Defended out loud
benchmarks.detail: A purple-team capstone - attack, detect, respond - defended for 30 minutes.

stages.title: Security foundations and ethics
stages.benchmark: Stanford CS155 (intro)  |  Berkeley CS161 (intro)  |  CompTIA Security+ objectives
stages.goal: Understand how attacks work, who does them, and the rules you work under.
stages.doneWhen: You can explain the main attack types and defences to a non-technical manager, and map a real breach to its causes.
stages.resources: Stanford CS155 and Berkeley CS161 notes (free)  |  CompTIA Security+ exam objectives
